title: Continuous cohorting scheduler: KV-thermal pressure mitigation for mixed-length workloads
creator: Maya R. Patel
description: Tune the continuous batching scheduler by introducing a cohorting admission strategy and KV thermal-pressure-aware pinning to reduce GPU memory pressure and P99 latency for mixed prompt/response workloads. The goal is to increase effective throughput while avoiding noisy eviction cascades during short-high/long-low traffic mixes.
context: We continue to see tail latency spikes and elevated KV eviction churn when workloads contain interleaved very short prompts (single-turn chat) and long responses (code generation / summarization). Existing continuous-batcher aggregates by length bins and time windows which causes frequent KV churn and GPU slab fragmentation under bursty traffic. Prior tickets explored length-aware bins and prefetching; this ticket focuses on dynamic cohorting (soft groups of requests with similar history) and a thermal-pressure heuristic that slows admissions and pins hot KV slices when GPU memory occupancy trends toward high fragmentation/thermal headroom limits.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement a light-weight cohort assignment in the continuous scheduler: requests are assigned to transient cohorts based on recent token-length distribution, latency budget, and model variant. Cohorts are small (4-12 concurrent slots) and have their own admission windows to reduce interleaving of extreme short/long sequences. 2) Add KV 'thermal' metrics (fragmentation_ratio, pin_score, eviction_rate) and surface them to the scheduler. 3) Introduce a soft-pin policy: when fragmentation_ratio > 0.65 OR eviction_rate > 0.12 for a GPU, prefer pinning hot KV slices for cohorts with high reuse and slow admission for cohorts causing churn. 4) Admission throttling: reduce cohort admission rate by up to 30% when predicted p99 would otherwise exceed SLO, fallback to smaller model variant or CPU-safe path for overflow. 5) Compatibility layer: ensure behavior is togglable via runtime flags and safe for Dedicated clusters. 6) Add metrics and dashboards for cohort hit-rate, per-cohort KV pin rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, and GPU slab fragmentation time series.
tradeoffs: Soft cohorting reduces worst-case interleaving but adds admission complexity and slightly increased average latency for some short-turn requests due to throttling.
Pinning hot KV slices reduces eviction churn but can increase steady-state GPU memory usage and reduce capacity per GPU; must be balanced with eviction thresholds.
Admission throttling can push load to lower-cost model variants, which may degrade output quality for a subset of requests—requires monitoring and configurable quality guardrails.
Cohort metadata increases scheduler state; we must ensure metadata lifetime is bounded to avoid scheduler memory growth.
Additional metrics increase cardinality in the console; we'll aggregate by cohort to limit cardinality.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment demonstrating >=10% reduction in p99 generation latency on mixed prompt/response synthetic workload compared to baseline continuous-batcher, holding p50 within +/-5%.
KV eviction_rate reduced by >=20% and fragmentation_ratio reduced by >=15% on the test cluster under representative traffic replay.
No regressions in throughput for homogeneous workloads (all-short or all-long) beyond 5%.
Feature is behind a runtime flag and can be toggled per-cluster; rollout plan documented.
Design doc and dashboard links included in ticket; at least one peer review from runtime and infra teams recorded.
